title: RayCAD operation template
description: One operation template of a library, the file templates/<uuid>.optemplate.json (PLAN.md 3.6, libraries.h OpTemplate): a saved operation with its tool query and parameters, keyed by the feature it is for. Values in toolQuery, params, heights, feeds may be expressions of the document's expression language over feature.* and tool.* (with or without a leading '$'; docs/template_expressions.md lists the names). The keys set, sequence, when, feeds and heights (task T-057) are read by src/cam/templates.h; src/lib keeps them in OpTemplate::extraJson. Unknown keys are allowed and are kept when RayCAD saves the template again.

schema.description: Version of this file's format. A larger value means a newer RayCAD wrote it.

material.description: Material id, or null for any.

machine.description: Machine id, or null for any.

toolQuery.description: A LibraryStack::queryTools query; numeric values may be expressions. Two more keys: 'prefer' ({field: expression}: the nearest of the tools that match) and 'id' (that exact tool).

params.description: Operation parameters as the operation type's schema defines them; a numeric parameter may be an expression.

set.description: The template set it belongs to ('Tapped holes'): the templates applied together in one action.

sequence.description: Its place in the set, ascending. Templates of a set with the same sequence are alternatives: each hole takes the first whose featureKind and 'when' match it.

when.description: Conditions on feature.* variables that must all hold: a number, a text or true/false is equality; an object takes min and max (inclusive), above and below (exclusive).

feeds.description: The feeds rule: 'calculated' (the feeds and speeds calculator for the tool, the setup's stock material and machine) or 'fixed' (rpm and feeds in mm/min, numbers or expressions). Absent: calculated.

opClass.description: calculated: the cutting data preset's class ('drill', 'tap', 'spot', 'ream'); empty lets the calculator choose.

heights.description: The heights rule: lengths in mm or expressions; the ones left out take the operation panel's defaults.
